title: Data Controls Routing Lattice for Customer Requests (logging redaction, retention, PII exports, audit exports)
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Goal: Build a deterministic, auditable routing lattice for non-bug customer requests related to data controls (logging redaction, retention policy changes, PII handling/export requests, and audit export requirements). This ticket defines the decision criteria, routing matrix, SLA targets, acceptance criteria, and recommended automation to consistently triage inbound enterprise requests.

Problem statement: Customers frequently request data governance changes via support and CSM channels. Current handling is ad-hoc, causing slow responses, missed SLA expectations, unclear ownership between PM/Eng/Security, and inconsistent applied controls. We need a repeatable process + lightweight automation that: (1) classifies request type and sensitivity, (2) maps to teams and required approvals, (3) assigns priority and SLO, and (4) tracks audit trail and handoffs.

Scope (in/out): In-scope: request routing rules, decision lattice, acceptance criteria, required metadata templates, automation for ticket enrichment, and escalation paths. Out-of-scope: implementation of per-customer encryption key rotations (separate SEC/ENG project) and deep retention engine changes beyond configuration surface.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic routing lattice document exists and is reviewed by Eng + Security + Legal
A request intake template (support/CSM) with mandatory metadata is live in Zendesk/Playbook
Routing rules map request -> owner team -> required approvals (e.g., Security sign-off, Legal notice, Configuration change) for >=90% of historical sample requests
SLA matrix established: initial triage <=24h, decision <=5 business days for non-technical requests, engineering change estimated within agreed SLAs or escalated
Automation prototype enriches incoming tickets with customer tier, data classification, and known integrations (Confluence + internal mapping)
Audit trail fields are defined and surfaced in Console (request id, approver, decision, retention change applied)

notes: Trade-offs: Centralized routing engine reduces duplication but adds a single point of configuration; decided to implement light-weight rules with per-team override to mitigate operational risk.
Customer tiers: Enterprise customers should have expedited paths and optional custom agreements; include a flag in the intake template to mark custom SLA.
Data classification: Use existing classification taxonomy from SEC-77; map 'sensitive' requests to extra approvals and longer decision windows.
Fallback behavior: If routing rules are ambiguous, default to Security review + triage owner assigned to Support Ops for manual resolution.
